stories.headline: Rioters loot stores and throw Molotov cocktails in Frankfurt as Gen Z protests over living costs and the draft spread to Germany
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people marched in more than 30 German cities on Saturday, including Berlin and Frankfurt, in protests organized by the group Gen Z regelt ("Gen Z takes charge"), which wants more spending on schools, housing and climate and opposes plans to bring back mandatory military service. The mostly peaceful marches turned violent in places: Frankfurt police said shop windows were smashed in the city center and Molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency crews, and they urged bystanders to leave the area. In Hamburg some barricades were set on fire, and businesses had boarded up ahead of time. Official counts suggested turnout fell short of the 182,000 organizers expected. The unrest comes weeks after some of France's worst rioting in decades, and cost-of-living protests have also hit Italy, Serbia and Spain.

stories.headline: FBI agents start knocking on the doors of the 'other Dan Sullivan's' donors as the Alaska Senate probe widens
stories.summary: The FBI has begun contacting donors to Dan J. Sullivan, the Alaska Senate candidate who shares a name with Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, asking whether they were deceived, the Associated Press reports. Agents have reached donors in at least two remote Alaska communities and a couple in Massachusetts; in Petersburg, the fishing town where the candidate lives, an agent left a card at a boat dealership owned by Charles Flint, who gave $500 and asked whether he had been "misled." Flint said he wasn't and plans to rank Democrat Mary Peltola first and Dan J. Sullivan second. Alaska U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman has said the investigation has run for months but surged after reports that Peltola's campaign helped recruit the retired teacher. The Justice Department is also seeking a court order to set aside ballots that rank him; Alaska's Republican-led state government called that demand "meritless" and impossible without breaking ballot secrecy.

stories.headline: Trumbull High's Golden Eagle Marching Band wins the Class III Open state championship and sweeps the caption awards
stories.summary: The Trumbull High School Golden Eagle Marching Band is the 2026 Class III Open Connecticut state champion, the town announced Saturday evening. The band scored 88.1 and also took home the awards for Best Music, Best Color Guard, Best Overall Effect and Best Percussion. "Trumbull is very proud of you!" the town said in its congratulations.

stories.headline: Crosby ties Marcel Dionne on the all-time points list, but the Penguins fall 5-4 in Montreal as the Canadiens win a fifth straight
stories.summary: Josh Anderson scored twice and added an assist, and the Montreal Canadiens held on to beat the Penguins 5-4 at Bell Centre on Saturday for their fifth straight win. Sidney Crosby had a goal and two assists; his goal with 3:11 left pulled Pittsburgh within one and tied Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL's career points list at 1,771, and his assist on Erik Karlsson's first-period power-play goal made him the league's all-time assist leader with a single team. Montreal blocked three shots in the final minute, including one by Anderson on a Karlsson blast with 50 seconds left, and Jacob Fowler made 25 saves for his seventh straight win. Karlsson had a goal and two assists, and Rickard Rakell and Tommy Novak each had a goal and an assist for Pittsburgh (5-7-2). "We needed to be better at just kind of controlling momentum," coach Dan Muse said.

stories.headline: Jets put DT T'Vondre Sweat on injured reserve and promote Payton Page ahead of today's 1 p.m. game against the Raiders
stories.summary: The Jets placed defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat on injured reserve Saturday and signed defensive tackle Payton Page to the active roster before Sunday's 1 p.m. home game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Sweat, who came from Tennessee in February in a swap for Jermaine Johnson, had played in all seven games with 17 tackles and two tackles for loss. Page, an undrafted Clemson product who first signed in 2025, played every preseason game this summer. The team also elevated offensive lineman Brant Banks and edge rusher Quinton Bell, a former Raiders draft pick, from the practice squad for the game. The 2-5 Jets are trying to snap a run of close losses against a Raiders team that has dropped four straight.

stories.headline: Golden State Valkyries win the WNBA title in only their second season, beating Atlanta 68-63 in the first Game 7 in Finals history
stories.summary: The Golden State Valkyries won their first WNBA championship Saturday with a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7, the first seven-game Finals decider in league history. Gabby Williams led Golden State with 30 points, four blocks and three steals. "All we heard last year: We don't have no stars, we don't have no talent," she said afterward. "Yeah right. We got good people. We got winners." Jordin Canada scored 18 for Atlanta, while Angel Reese was held to 8 points on 3-of-7 shooting; the Dream are now winless in four Finals trips. The title caps a record WNBA season: 3.8 million fans attended regular-season games, and ESPN, ABC and CBS all had their most-watched seasons ever.

stories.headline: 17 Disney World and Universal employees are among 281 people arrested in a Florida child-predator and trafficking sting
stories.summary: Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said a seven-day undercover operation targeting human trafficking and adults seeking sex with children led to 281 arrests, including 13 Disney employees and four Universal Studios employees. Judd said 31 suspects traveled to the county expecting to have sex with a child, 24 brought guns to the meetings, nine were on probation and 32 were in the country illegally, 16 of whom have been turned over to ICE. Those arrested include a youth football coach for kids 11 to 14, an active-duty Navy sailor, a former Disney Mickey Mouse character performer and a Disney worker who had his uniform in his car. The sheriff said Disney cooperated with investigators and has fired all the employees involved.

stories.headline: A hidden AirTag leads police to an Easton state rep's house, and she's charged with stealing her GOP opponent's lawn sign
stories.summary: State Rep. Anne Hughes, D-Easton, was given a summons Saturday on a misdemeanor sixth-degree larceny charge after her Republican challenger's lawn sign was tracked to her property by a hidden AirTag. Darrell Harris said a volunteer frustrated by disappearing signs had hidden trackers in some of them, and one pinged Friday at Hughes' home; Easton police showed up there at 10 p.m. The signs mocked Hughes for a "hot mic" moment in which she joked, "We're not rich. But I always tell the governor to tax my people — they won't even notice." Hughes, seeking a fifth term in the 135th District (Easton, Redding and Weston), admitted removing signs she says were improperly placed on public property, apologized, and said she takes "full responsibility." She is due in court in two weeks.

stories.headline: Apple Watch still an hour off after the clocks fell back? Apple posts a quick fix for the Always On bug
stories.summary: Apple has published a support note for Apple Watch owners whose watch still shows the wrong hour after daylight saving time ended early Sunday. Apple says the incorrect time appears only on the Always On display while your wrist is down; when you tap the screen or raise your wrist, it jumps to the correct hour. The fix is to switch to a different watch face and then back again, or simply restart the watch. MacRumors notes that users in Europe saw the same glitch when their clocks went back in late October.

stories.headline: Apple Maps quietly starts blurring NASA launch sites and Space Force and Air Force bases, while Google Maps does not
stories.summary: Apple Maps has begun blurring satellite imagery of a number of sensitive U.S. sites, with no announcement, Space Explored reports. Now hidden are NASA and Space Force locations including Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Vandenberg Space Force Base, Wallops Flight Facility and Stennis Space Center, along with bomber bases such as Whiteman (home of the B-2) and Ellsworth (B-1B). The rollout is uneven: big Navy installations like Pearl Harbor and Norfolk, Dyess Air Force Base and the B-52 base at Barksdale are still visible. Google Maps has not blurred any of these sites, and the site expects Apple to keep adding more bases.

stories.headline: Deep Purple cancel two German shows after singer Ian Gillan is hospitalized with a medical emergency
stories.summary: Deep Purple have called off two shows on the German leg of their "Splat!" world tour, Saturday night at the QI Arena in Leipzig and Sunday at the Sporthalle in Hamburg, after a medical emergency put singer Ian Gillan in the hospital. The band did not give details on Gillan's condition but said it shares fans' disappointment and is working to reschedule both dates, with existing tickets valid for the new shows. Gillan, 81, has fronted the band in its best-known lineups since 1969. Bassist Roger Glover said in July that the band has no plans for a farewell tour: "We ain't gonna stop."

stories.headline: James Hetfield says Metallica asked Turnstile to open on the M72 tour, and the band said no
stories.summary: Metallica's James Hetfield says the band invited Baltimore punk band Turnstile to open on their M72 world tour, and Turnstile turned them down. "We have seen them live, we wanted to get them on tour, and they said no. They're doing good on their own already," Hetfield said on his "Riff Life" radio show, adding that he's a fan and urging people to see them live. Turnstile's 2025 album "Never Enough" reached No. 9 on the U.S. Billboard chart, and the band recently brought death metal veterans Obituary out as an opener. Metallica are in the middle of a residency at the Las Vegas Sphere and resume the M72 tour in 2027.

stories.headline: Ukraine says Russia lost a record 54,400 troops in October, its worst month since the full-scale invasion began
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff says Russia lost an estimated 54,400 soldiers killed or wounded in October, 8,170 more than in September and the highest monthly toll since the 2022 invasion. Kyiv says the rate now outpaces Moscow's ability to replace its troops. Ukraine's Azov corps said much of the toll came from Russia's push toward Dobropillia in Donetsk Oblast, where it claims more than 6,800 Russian troops were killed, wounded or captured, and drone forces commander Robert "Magyar" Brovdi said his units hit a Russian soldier every 159 seconds. Ukraine's figures can't be independently verified. Russia announced plans on Oct. 2 to call up 120,000 more conscripts. Overnight, Russian strikes on power plants in four regions again left hundreds of thousands of families without electricity.

stories.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 5,000 deaths, now the second deadliest ever, with no vaccine for this strain
stories.summary: Deaths in Congo's Ebola outbreak have passed 5,000, government data showed Saturday: 5,026 people have died out of 10,351 infected, a fatality rate near 50%. That makes it the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak in history, behind only the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that killed about 11,000. The outbreak, declared in mid-May, is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved vaccine or treatment. It has reached 67 of Congo's 178 health zones, mostly in Ituri and North Kivu in the east, and cases have turned up in other African countries, including Kenya and Nigeria. A WHO official called it "a very tragic milestone."

stories.headline: With no shuttle left to reach it, NASA asks private companies how to boost or service the sinking Hubble telescope
stories.summary: NASA has asked the commercial space industry for ideas on how to save the Hubble Space Telescope, which is slowly losing altitude and is expected to fall back into the atmosphere sometime in the early to mid-2030s. In a request for information issued Oct. 29, the agency asked companies to describe current or near-future capabilities for safely capturing Hubble and raising its orbit, servicing it, or, failing that, carrying out a controlled disposal. Space shuttles once boosted and repaired the 36-year-old observatory, most recently with a nudge from Columbia in 2002, but the shuttle fleet is retired and NASA has no spacecraft of its own that can do the job.

stories.headline: LEGO reveals its first Technic set of 2027: a hand-cranked Solar System with all eight planets in orbit for $99.99
stories.summary: LEGO has officially announced 42254 Solar System Planets in Orbit, the first LEGO Technic set of 2027. The 572-piece model goes on sale Jan. 1 for $99.99 and expands on 42179 Planet Earth and Moon in Orbit, which retires later this year. Turning a hand crank drives gears that send all eight planets around the sun at different speeds, and the base includes informational plaques. Jupiter and Saturn are printed elements, and Saturn's rings use what appears to be a new transparent foil or textile piece.

stories.headline: Jeep's retro Gladiator Rewind, with arcade-style graphics and 8-bit embossed seats, is back for 2027
stories.summary: The Jeep Gladiator Rewind package returns for the 2027 model year, giving buyers another shot at the retro-styled pickup that debuted for 2026 after a concept at the 2025 Easter Jeep Safari. Bright angular '80s and '90s-style decals run along the sides, hood, fenders and tailgate, with body-color fender flares and grille, 17-inch machined wheels with gold pockets, bronze tow hooks and a gray-and-bronze Trail Rated badge. Inside, black Nappa leather seats are embossed with 8-bit-style patterns, with colorful stitching and Ice Blue and Plum accents. Mopar Insiders spotted 2027 examples in Anvil, Bright White, Black, Granite Crystal and Hydro Blue.

stories.headline: An English town wants King Charles to pardon the women it hanged as witches 400 years ago
stories.summary: Councilors in Maidstone, a town in southern England where records show more than 20 women convicted of witchcraft were hanged in the 1600s, are lobbying the U.K. government and plan to petition King Charles III for an official pardon. Around 5,000 people convicted of witchcraft, most of them women, were executed by hanging or burning across England and Scotland, often single women or widows blamed for natural disasters, illness or dead livestock. "It matters because it was a miscarriage of justice," councilor Claire Kehily told CBS News. While everyone accused in the 1690s Salem trials in Massachusetts has since been pardoned, not one convicted witch in the U.K. has been exonerated.

stories.headline: Overnight repaving on Route 111 (Main Street) in Trumbull will start after the polls close on Election Day
stories.summary: The Connecticut Department of Transportation will mill and resurface a short stretch of Route 111 (Main Street) in Trumbull between Whalburn Avenue and Chestnut Hill Road, the town said Friday. To avoid traffic trouble on Election Day, crews from Waters Construction won't start until the polls close on Tuesday, Nov. 3, and will work overnight to finish on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Drivers should expect lane closures on that 0.09-mile segment, with traffic control personnel, signs and local police guiding motorists through the work zone. CTDOT says the schedule could change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions and asks drivers to keep their speed down in the area.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: early voting’s final week at the library, a Town Hall Halloween parade for preschoolers, and a Hillcrest update
stories.summary: Early voting runs its final week in the Trumbull Library Community Room, 33 Quality St., from Monday, Oct. 26, through Sunday, Nov. 1. Hours are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., extended to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. On Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 10 and 11:30 a.m., Town Hall staff host a costume parade and trick-or-treating past decorated office doors for registered Trumbull kids ages 0 to 5. Each session is limited to 20 children. That evening the Hillcrest Middle School Building Committee gets project updates and the EMS Commission reviews vehicles, staffing and plans for Trumbull EMS’s 50th anniversary. The Conservation Commission meets Wednesday on tree rules and a spring 2027 tree giveaway.
